title: Mildred's legacy: Helen Humes and Rosemary Clooney
summary: Dance and Norvo talk about singers who sound like Mildred, including Helen Humes and Rosemary Clooney, and Norvo's Australian tour with Helen.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Yes, oh, boy. Well listen, well maybe we have said some of the things we want to say about -- about Mildred and her performance. I think one of the things we started to say when we didn't have the tape on -- was simply that, you know, she's never been giventhe credit, since. And it wasn't fashbnable or something. And you said, 'Well she never had the success she should've had while she was alive.' And perhaps she's never had the credit since. But I do think, Red, that over and over and over again, people do throw back to Mildred. I mean people come and say, who's this little rock girl, gosh I've forgotten her name now -- that was recording she had Benny Carter accompany her -- (Maria Muldaur-ed.)

Sings like Mildred and you'll hear -- and then people say, Helen Hume sounds like Mildred -- Helen does sound like Mildred quite often, I often hear her sound like Mildred -- I think -- to myself, now, did those two gals listen to each other at times, appreciate each other, or did one -- be inspired, I wonder or do they both just have that same little something --
-- maybe they do, I don't know in Helen's case. I don't even know who knew whom first. In Helen and Mildred's case. I think they just have the same lilting, high voice and gay sort of --
Well, I think it's a pitch where the voice was. I think Helen's pitch has a tendency there.
I tell you, Rosemary Clooney has the same kind of pitch.

She'd done a couple of records where I just happened to be in -- walking to the car or something and turned the radio on and hear the end of it, or hear part of it and it shook me for a minute. She'd be in a (unintelligible high register) and it'd be so much like Mildred.
And it'd be -- yet somebody from Cincinnati where they were raised, the two girls, they'd say, that Mildred was the one they listened to when they were young.
I don't know if this is so or not. I know Rosemary -- I don't know, I suppose I could ask her, she'd be honest and say yes, or no.
-- there's a certain way that she had a singing with phrases, I think -- course I -- I like Helen, I worked with Helen after -- later and --
She told me you took her abroad, didn't you?
You took her abroad, you took her to Australia --
Yes, we went to Australia, we had some fun, we made some records together. Big band records --
In fact I used -- I use some of the charts that Eddie made for Mildred.
Oh, yeah. For Victor. That's an album that Victor brought out under her name, now.
With Red Norvo's orchestra, it was mine, originally, see --
So we turned it around and we brought it out on Helen, which is fine, which is all right.

Well ah -- well I'm really saying is that regardless, Mildred set standards that people do still keep referring to. I mean, every now and then a singer comes up and people say, 'like Mildred,' you know, or some --
Oh, I get it all the time, you know?
Oh, yeah people know the band we had and all that sort of thing.
